title: Network Interruption Handling
description: Handle network interruptions gracefully with retry logic, backoff, and offline detection in React Query.

data.text: Mobile users regularly experience network drops, flaky connections, captive portals, and spotty coverage. React Query provides built-in retry logic out of the box, but production applications need more nuanced handling: exponential backoff to reduce server load, offline detection to adjust behavior, and graceful UI states that keep users informed without alarm.

data.title: Design for Failure
data.text: Assume the network will fail at some point. Good offline handling makes your app feel reliable even on poor connections. Show cached data, queue mutations, and inform the user â€” never leave them staring at a broken error screen.

React Query retries failed queries automatically. The default is 3 retries with exponential backoff. You can customize this with a `retry` function that decides whether to retry based on the error, and a `retryDelay` function that controls the wait between attempts.

rows: Retry failed queries on component mount

data.title: Custom retry logic with exponential backoff
data.content: Custom retry function that skips 404 and 401 errors but retries transient failures with backoff.

data.caption: Retry decision flow: when to retry, when to stop, and how backoff works.

data.text: The browser provides `navigator.onLine` to detect connectivity status, but it is not always reliable. Pair it with React Query's `networkMode` option and event listeners for `online` and `offline` events to build a robust offline detection system.

data.title: Offline detection hook
data.content: A simple custom hook that tracks online/offline status and shows a banner when offline.

data.title: Graceful Degradation
data.text: When offline, show cached data with a clear indication that it may be outdated. Allow users to read and interact with cached content. Prevent mutations that will fail, or queue them for later.

React Query v5 introduced `networkMode` to control query behavior when offline. Set it to `'offlineFirst'` to use cached data when offline and skip the network request entirely. Set it to `'always'` to attempt refetching regardless of connection status.

data.title: Using networkMode for offline-first queries
data.content: networkMode: 'offlineFirst' prevents failed network requests when offline.

data.title: Exercise: Build an Offline-Aware Todo App
data.description: Add network interruption handling to a todo app. Show an offline banner, prevent mutations when offline, and retry with backoff.
steps: Create a useOnlineStatus hook using navigator.onLine and event listeners.
Show an offline banner when isOnline is false.
Disable the add-todo button when offline, with a tooltip explaining why.
Configure retry with exponential backoff for the todos query.
Add a retry count display next to the error message.
data.expectedOutcome: Users see an offline banner when disconnected, cannot submit when offline, and queries retry with visible backoff when the network is unstable.

items.question: Is navigator.onLine reliable?
items.answer: It reports the browser's network status, but it can be inaccurate. A user might be on a network that blocks specific domains. Use it as a signal, not a guarantee. Always handle query errors gracefully regardless of the reported status.

items.question: What is the difference between networkMode and retry?
items.answer: networkMode controls whether React Query attempts a network request at all (e.g., skipping it when offline). retry controls what happens after a request fails â€” whether to try again and how many times.

items.question: Should I show retry counts to users?
items.answer: For critical data, showing a subtle retry indicator helps users understand that the app is working. For non-critical data, silent retries are usually better UX.

data.title: Network Interruption Key Points
points: Retry logic with exponential backoff handles transient failures gracefully.
navigator.onLine combined with event listeners provides offline detection.
Show cached data and communicate status clearly to users.
data.takeaway: Robust network handling makes your app feel reliable even on poor connections.
